newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar off highs in Tokyo after topping 1.83 marks.
newsitem.headline: Dollar off highs in Tokyo after topping 1.83 marks.

text.p: 0645 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar slipped from its highs against the mark by late Tokyo on Thursday, but was still above its New York close. Mark/yen trade led activity, dealers said.

The dollar slipped after it failed to stay above 1.83 marks as Japanese institutional investors and U.S. securities firms' bids protected the mark vs the yen, which was a key factor putting a lid on the dollar's gains versus the mark, they said.
Dealers said the mark was bought back by those operators at around 63.10/20 yen.
One dealer said operators actively unwound positions in the dollar against the mark after seeing heavy dollar selling orders by European banks above 1.8320/30 marks.

Earlier in the afternoon, the mark came under strong selling pressure, sending the dollar above 1.83 marks, after U.S. operators sold the German currency against the yen in large volumes, dealers said.
At 0659 GMT, the mark stood at 63.47/50 yen compared with 63.42 yen in early Asian trade.
The dollar closed at 115.62/72 yen and 1.8255/65 marks in New York on Wednesday.
Dealers said they were cautiously watching for possible mark-supportive comments from Bundesbank officials after the bank's council meeting scheduled for later in the day.

"Mark/yen activity led the market. That is the latest trend during Tokyo trading hours," a Japanese city bank spot dealer said. "The underlying bearishness of the mark still remained intact, but we have to watch out for possible comments by Bundesbank officials after the meeting today."

Dealers said there were rumours that the Bundesbank had placed orders to sell dollars for commercial purposes, and such rumours were a factor in pushing down the greenback from a high of 1.8325 marks set in London overnight.

The dollar/yen rate was locked in tight boxed ranges with heavy offers by exporters lined up above 116 yen, while bids by Japanese investment trust supported the greenback around 115.60/70 yen, dealers said.
A European bank dealer in Singapore said the dollar/yen rate was likely to remain confined in a range of 115.50 to 116.00.
Dealers said the market ignored the release of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly economic outlook.
The BOJ said Japan's economy is continuing on a moderate recovery trend supported by the yen's depreciation until early last spring and the expansion of information-related demand.

"The impact of the BOJ's report on the currency market was limited, although Japanese market interest rates fell as the market took the report as showing a weak economic outlook in Japan," a Japanese trust bank dealer said. ---Singapore newsroom +65-870-3080 ---Chikafumi Hodo, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
